spec-grapher-modernization-master.title: Grapher modernization master implementation order
spec-grapher-modernization-master.content: Canonical modernization directive: evolve Grapher surgically into a general-purpose lifecycle-, truth-, provenance-, scope-, evidence-, and verification-aware work graph. Preserve v1 compatibility and history; use schema v2, atomic journaled mutations, finalized records, truth-aware retrieval, generation-aware multi-agent state, checkpoints, non-destructive compaction, deep media ingest, updated Cursor guidance, and one normalized model shared by CLI and Dash. Grapher records identity and attestation but does not authenticate actors or orchestrate agents.

finding-grapher-modernization-v030.title: Grapher 0.3 modernization implemented
finding-grapher-modernization-v030.content: Grapher 0.3 implements expanded general and multi-agent registries; normalized scope/provenance/evidence/finalization fields; stable content-only vector identity; attestation-gated verified provenance; finalized-record protections; fsync-backed atomic writes with rollback-on-journal-failure; append-only mutation history across CLI, migration, curation, checkpoints, transfer, ingest, and Agent Hub services; lossless validated v1 migration with backups; intent-, truth-, provenance-, and generation-aware search with explainable factors; strict scope filters; comprehensive validation/audit including supersession/dependency cycles, evidence gaps, stale checkpoints, deep-ingest quality, and generation ambiguity; review-first checkpoint refresh and compaction; upgraded Cursor guidance; provenance/lifecycle Dash views, filters, semantic layouts, details, health, and non-canonical exports; generic museum, CASSIO, and multi-agent control fixtures. Non-embedding regression suite passes 45 tests.

spec-grapher-provenance-readiness.title: Grapher provenance and future training readiness addendum
spec-grapher-provenance-readiness.content: Canonical addendum to the modernization specification. Grapher must answer both current canonical state and how it came to exist. Meaningful graph mutations retain structured transition history with stable IDs, affected entities, typed changes, before/after values, timestamps, model-agnostic actor/source classification, rationale, attributable evidence, related decisions and requirements, supersession or override references, and operation correlation. Decisions, later outcomes, proposed actions, execution, observation, verification, and final canonical state remain distinct. Current state stays efficient and history is complementary. Preserve keyed-node and migration compatibility. Do not build ML or training functionality, model-specific fields, prompts, quality labels, or transcript hoards.

req-structured-state-transitions.title: Preserve structured graph state transitions
req-structured-state-transitions.content: Every meaningful mutation records immutable field- or relation-level transitions. Records include a stable transition ID, affected entity, event type, previous and resulting value, timestamp, actor/source, optional rationale and evidence references, related decision and requirement IDs, supersession/override transition IDs, and a shared operation ID. Covered changes include workflow, verification, truth status, lifecycle, decisions and requirements, evidence, blockers, dependencies, incidents/deviations, checkpoints, and canonical truth.

req-distinct-decision-outcome-phases.title: Keep decisions outcomes and action phases distinct
req-distinct-decision-outcome-phases.content: A decision such as request verification must remain distinct from later failed verification, revision, and passed verification outcomes. Proposed, executed, observed, verified, and canonical phases must not be silently converted into each other; each remains independently reconstructable in history.

req-attributable-actors-evidence-overrid.title: Attribute actors evidence and overrides
req-attributable-actors-evidence-overrid.content: Transition provenance distinguishes human, agent, system/tool, and migration/import sources without an LLM-specific identity model. Evidence retains source attribution when available; an agent report is not automatically equivalent to independent verification. Overrides retain original and overriding transitions, actor, rationale, and resulting state rather than deleting prior records.

constraint-provenance-not-ml-pipeline.title: Record operational history without building ML
constraint-provenance-not-ml-pipeline.content: Grapher records facts, states, transitions, provenance, evidence, and outcomes. It must not fine-tune models, add model-specific fields or prompts, label decisions good or bad, assume a model architecture, become an ML pipeline, or retain enormous conversations for speculative training. A downstream system may later transform selected records.

finding-grapher-provenance-v040.title: Grapher 0.4 structured provenance implemented
finding-grapher-provenance-v040.content: Grapher 0.4 keeps v1/v2 canonical graph reads unchanged and records structured, immutable transition arrays in the separate JSONL journal. save_graph_mutation now diffs nodes and edges into stable typed transitions with before/after values, model-agnostic actor kind, proposed/executed/observed/verified/canonical phase, rationale, evidence refs, related decisions and requirements, overrides/supersession, and operation correlation. Dependency, blocker, evidence, supersession, truth, workflow, verification, lifecycle, finalization, node, and general relation events are typed. Legacy hash-only records remain readable. grapher history queries by entity, operation, or event type; audit validates the journal. Evidence types now explicitly cover command output, human observation, agent reports, external artifacts, and Grapher-derived state. README documents the model. Full non-embedding suite passes 49 tests.

finding-grapher-hardening-v041.title: Grapher hardening v0.4.1 closes finalized-record and mutation-attribution gaps
finding-grapher-hardening-v041.content: September 3, 2026 hardening pass against docs/grapher-hardening-instructions.txt. Finalized records are now semantically immutable across add/update, direct provenance rewrites are blocked, ordinary remove_node deletion is forbidden for finalized records, and curate supersede preserves finalized historical records while attaching a new correction edge. Mutation authorship now propagates through CLI mutation commands, Agent Hub integration paths, and cassio curation journaling without collapsing known actors to system_tool. Ingest journaling now records created_stubs correctly. Added adversarial coverage for major finalized-field rewrites, finalized deletion prevention, supersession preservation, context-derived actor attribution, CLI actor propagation, Agent Hub create/update labeling, and integration relationship attribution. Targeted verification passed 55/55 tests.

finding-grapher-v041-release-hardening.title: Grapher 0.4.1 release hardening closes audited finalized-delete policy gap
finding-grapher-v041-release-hardening.content: September 3, 2026 follow-up hardening pass. Package/version metadata was bumped to 0.4.1 in pyproject, module version, egg-info metadata, and uv lock root package entry. The raw remove_node(force=True) administrative escape hatch was eliminated. Finalized-record forced deletion now exists only as an explicit audited CLI path via grapher rm --force-finalized, which requires actor attribution and a reason, records an administrative journal entry, and distinguishes node_removed_administratively from ordinary removal. Added one policy test covering denied unaudited forced deletion plus allowed journaled administrative deletion. Full suite result on the post-change tree: 78 passed in 3.44s on Python 3.12.3.
